components.description: The same chip the Origin 200 uses, on the IO-8 assembly at PCI device 4. On the Origin 300 it exposes serial A and B, the parallel function, the byte-bus Timekeeper and the board's 10/100 Ethernet, and no keyboard or mouse controller. No rear-panel parallel connector is established by the reviewed IO-8 connector inventory. The chip includes its one-wire engine, but this board does not fit the IOC3 Ethernet-address identity part: the address comes from the brick EEPROM through the L1. Serial A is the guest console; serial B is the second rear-panel serial port. Emulator chardev index 0 is reserved for the separate L1 management channel, with IOC3 A and B on indexes 1 and 2. The integration contract uses explicit population mask 0x17 and selects M48T35-compatible timekeeper-kind 1 as a documented compatibility choice whose clearance depends on the required Origin 300 qtest.

identity.notes: Function 00:04.0 and PCI revision 1 are observed. The exact IP45 subsystem device field is not observed. An Origin 300 configuration-space capture replaces the placeholder.

machine.name: Origin 300
machine.notes: One chassis is one Bedrock node with its NUMAlink 3 port cabled to nothing, so the fabric defers as CrayLink does on a one-node Origin 200. The board has no Crossbow chip, but the XBridge's own crossbar section is live: real Origin 300s report widget 0 as a crossbar (ASIC XBOW Rev 2) with the two PCI bridges at widgets 14 and 15, and a verbose PROM trace from one shows the Bedrock entering the crossbar at port 0xa (the captures listed in docs/library/boot-logs.md). One published two-CPU board reports node inventory IP45_2CPU, part 030-1780-001 rev C, with processors A and C installed; the owner's manual and the scan-tools field guide both also name a four-processor configuration (108-0263-004's own "IP45 4 CPU R14K 500MHZ 2MB" FRU name), which fits the two remaining slots B and D on the same two processor interfaces. Other captured IP45 boards are 030-1779-001 rev C (500 MHz) and 030-1797-001 rev B (600 MHz), with IO-8 boards 030-1673-003. A second chassis over the NUMAlink cable is a later configuration and out of scope; one owner's two cabled Origin 300s appear as modules 001c01 and 001c02 at nasids 0 and 1, and OpenBSD trapped on them (the OpenBSD captures).
